title: How Many Korean Households Have Just One Person?
context: Living alone is an increasingly visible part of life in Korea.
question: In 2024, roughly what share of South Korea's general households consisted of just one person?

feedbackByOption.A: This is much lower than the reported share of one-person general households.
feedbackByOption.C: The reported share was approximately 36.1% in 2024, subject to verification against the original official table.
feedbackByOption.D: This is higher than the reported share.

insight: This measures households, not the share of all people living alone.

title: The High-Five That Didn't Happen
context: Someone working in Korea tried to high-five a coworker, but received a fist bump instead. Another coworker smiled rather than shaking hands.
question: What would you make of these reactions?

options.text: They might prefer less physical contact.
Those greetings might feel out of place at work.
Maybe they were uncomfortable with me personally.

reveal: Replies offered different interpretations: one suggested that physical greetings can feel uncomfortable between people who aren't close; another said high-fives felt childish and handshakes too formal in some casual settings. Neither coworker's actual intention was established.
insight: A friendly gesture can carry different social meanings depending on the person and setting. These replies are individual perspectives, not universal rules.

sources.notes: Earlier manually collected dataset rows R098–R100; original permalink must be recovered before publishing.
